claims.text: The as-cast HfNbTaTiZr baseline is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The constituent elements in the as-cast baseline are statistically randomly distributed.
A controlled heat treatment can induce measurable SRO in HfNbTaTiZr without producing secondary phases.
The appropriate controlled comparison is between random and SRO-enhanced HfNbTaTiZr samples tested under identical conditions.
SRO further enhances local lattice distortion within the BCC lattice.
SRO-generated local atomic configurations create dislocation-pinning sites.
SRO restricts edge-dislocation glide in HfNbTaTiZr.
Reduced dislocation mobility produces less elevated-temperature softening and a plateau-like yield-strength response.
The SRO-enhanced alloy will retain higher or more stable yield strength than the random baseline at elevated temperature.
Restricted dislocation mobility caused by SRO reduces and homogenizes thermal expansion.
The SRO-enhanced alloy will have a lower thermal expansion coefficient than the random baseline.
SRO and inhibited dislocation mobility make the elevated-temperature elastic response more isotropic.
The SRO-enhanced alloy will show less directional variation in elastic moduli than the random baseline.
The predicted responses should hold from approximately 600 K to 1073 K under quasi-static or nanoindentation loading where dislocation-mediated plasticity dominates.
The hypothesis may cease to apply when phase transformations or kinetic roughening dominate.
Existing information is insufficient to predict quantitative changes in strength retention, thermal expansion, elastic isotropy, or the optimal SRO-inducing heat treatment.
